artifacts.summary: Nine-phase plan (11.5h) building the advisory CARRIED-UNVERIFIED source-naming check, recording both reasoned exclusions, and landing the three convention amendments plus redeploy.

memory_candidates.content: When a shell check greps for a mandated literal token across a document corpus, the densest source of false positives is the documents that DISCUSS the token rather than use it: a backticked bare token, a grep command literal, and a regex literal all match the token pattern but are mentions, not instances. Measured on one real artifact: 13 opening-token occurrences against 8 complete bracket matches, where 9 of the 13 were mentions. Two literal, cheap discriminators suppress them all without any semantic judgment: skip an occurrence whose token is immediately preceded by a backtick or a backslash. Pair this with a bounded match window, because flattening newlines before matching (needed so a line-wrapped instance is not missed) otherwise lets one unclosed mention consume text up to an arbitrarily distant later bracket, absorbing and hiding a genuinely malformed instance that follows. A token-mention suppression case and a hide-the-following-instance case belong in the fixture suite of any such check.
